classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a function evaluated at |x|, find exact graph intersections, and reject an impossible negative value of |x|.

content.prompt: Let $f(x)=x^2-4x$. Find the values of $x$ where $f(|x|)\le3$.

answer.worked:
$f(|x|)=x^2-4|x|$. Sketch this graph and $y=3$. Their intersections satisfy
$$\begin{align*}x^2-4|x|&=3\\(|x|-2)^2&=7\\|x|-2&=\pm\sqrt7\\|x|&=2\pm\sqrt7\\|x|&=2+\sqrt7\\x&=\pm(2+\sqrt7).\end{align*}$$
The value $2-\sqrt7$ is negative and cannot equal $|x|$. The graph is on or below $y=3$ between its two intersections:
$$-2-\sqrt7\le x\le2+\sqrt7.$$

spec.description: Symmetric graph of f(|x|) with its two valleys and the horizontal comparison line. Both boundary intersections are included.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2-4|x| and y=3 intersect at x=-(2+sqrt(7)) and x=2+sqrt(7).
